summary: AWS <-> GCP multi-account session tag encoding mismatch causing ephemeral access failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (internal dedicated onboarding jobs) intermittently fail to assume AWS roles via our federated bridge from GCP workload identity pools. Failures started after the recent bridge update (infra PR #8242) and manifest as AccessDenied when assuming role with session tags present.

Impact:
- Several Dedicated onboarding jobs cannot provision resources across accounts (approx 12% of attempts over last 48h).
- Affects ops/infra teams debugging dedicated onboarding; no customer-facing incidents yet but blocks private deployment demos.

Environment:
- prod (us-east) bridge service running in GKE, bridge version infra@v2026.03.08, recent config change: URL-encoding of tag payload enabled.
- Downstream AWS accounts: infra-prod-main, infra-dedicated-1.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From staging runner with GCP SA bound to WIF pool, request short-lived credentials via bridge (assume-role-with-web-identity flow).
2) Include session tags: {"team":"platform","job-id":"onboard-xxxx"} and custom attributes from GCP token.
3) Bridge forwards call to AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity including TagSpecification header; AWS responds with AccessDenied for some role ARNs.

Observed behavior:
- Bridge logs show session tag string is URL-encoded (percent-escapes applied) instead of plain UTF-8.
- CloudTrail for affected AWS accounts shows TagKeys present but TagValues truncated or containing literal percent encodings (e.g., "%7B" instead of "{").

Expected behavior:
- Tags forwarded to STS should be decoded to original values and attached to session as plain strings per AWS Tagging semantics.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally using a clipped WIF token; toggling the bridge flag that enabled payload encoding resolves failures.
- Hypothesis: An intermediate HTTP client library in the bridge started applying application/x-www-form-urlencoded encoding to the tag payload because of a content-type change introduced in infra PR #8242.
- Not all roles are impacted: roles with tag-based condition keys using StringEquals are sensitive to encoding; roles without tag conditions succeed.
- CloudTrail timestamps align with the deployment of infra@v2026.03.08 across primary cluster nodes.
- Related prior tickets: INT-314158 (permission coalescence), INT-947663 (assume-role chain failing for dedicated provisioning).

Logs/links:
- Bridge service logs (grep): /logs/bridge-prod/2026-03-12/encoded-tags-*.log (internal S3 link in Confluence runbook).
- CloudTrail snippets: see confluence page linked above.

Workaround:
- Roll bridge back to infra@v2026.03.05 or toggle the new encoding flag for the bridge service (deploy config: BRIDGE_ENCODE_TAGS=false) to restore original behavior.

Next steps / proposed fix:
1) Short-term: Toggle BRIDGE_ENCODE_TAGS=false in prod bridge config and confirm recovery for ongoing onboarding jobs (owner: SRE).
2) Mid-term: Update bridge HTTP client usage to send tag payload as JSON (Content-Type: application/json) and ensure no additional URL encoding is applied; add unit tests that exercise tag edge-cases (owner: infra team).
3) Add an e2e test to onboarding CI that asserts session tags arrive intact in a test AWS account.
4) Postmortem and rollout checklist to prevent similar regressions when bumping client libraries.

Acceptance criteria:
- No AccessDenied in STS when using session tags for 24h post-fix across all dedicated onboarding jobs.
- Deployment includes tests and a feature flag defaulted to false with clear rollout steps.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:42 - Aisha Patel: Initial report after two failed dedicated onboarding runs. Attached bridge logs and sample CloudTrail snippet.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Diego Morales: Reproduced locally, confirmed tag payloads were percent-encoded. Created temporary rollback patch and tested against infra-dedicated-1 account (success).

2026-03-11 11:05 - SRE Oncall (Lena Chen): Toggled BRIDGE_ENCODE_TAGS=false in prod canary (node pool A). Observed onboarding job success on canary. Will roll to remaining nodes after validation window.

2026-03-12 16:30 - Infra Engineer (Marco Ruiz): Root cause identified: upgraded http-client library started auto-encoding form data for request bodies with content-type omitted. Opened PR to set explicit Content-Type and add tests (PR #8301).

2026-03-14 08:00 - Diego Morales: Coordinating rollout of PR #8301. Preparing CI e2e to assert decoded tags via temporary test role. Blocking: need cross-account CloudTrail test role created by infra-admins (see linked issue INT-947663).
resolution: Investigation ongoing. Temporary mitigation applied (BRIDGE_ENCODE_TAGS=false) and canary rollout successful. Infra PR #8301 prepared to set explicit JSON content-type and add tests; awaiting cross-account test role creation and final review before full rollout.
notes: Do not apply blanket policy changes to AWS roles as a workaround; issue is in bridge encoding behavior.
Add a monitoring alert that detects percent-encoding patterns in outgoing tag payloads (SRE task).
Consider signing a small runbook for dedicated onboarding that lists the feature flag and rollback steps.
